source.title: Gradient Descent Finds Global Minima of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: S. Du; J. Lee; Hao-Chuan Li; Li-Wei Wang; Xi-Yu Zhai

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and symbols are garbled in extraction, but the main theorem statements are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence of gradient descent to zero training loss for randomly initialized overparameterized networks, using a different setting and theoretical measure from the claim versions’ benchmark classification results.
record.gate_note: The reported results are theorem guarantees, not empirical benchmark runs. The paper states that it studies training loss, not test loss; it also notes that its required widths are very large and its analysis covers gradient descent rather than stochastic gradient descent. Related-work results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves convergence of squared training loss under sufficient width and step-size assumptions. It does not establish any version as stated: it reports neither benchmark classification error nor actual depth degradation, and differences between sufficient convergence bounds do not demonstrate differences in training outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as a statement of sufficient theoretical guarantees: randomly initialized gradient descent drives squared training loss toward zero geometrically for sufficiently overparameterized fully connected, residual, and convolutional residual networks, with polynomial depth dependence for the residual architectures. The authors leave practical widths and stochastic gradient descent unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proves convergence for least-squares loss with smooth, analytic, non-polynomial activations and full-batch gradient descent. It does not run classification benchmarks; its theoretical ResNet uses a skip connection at every layer and explicit residual scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture changes the width and step-size dependence on depth: fully-connected networks have exponential depth dependence in the analysis, while residual and convolutional residual networks have polynomial dependence.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomly initialized full-batch gradient descent has a geometric squared-loss convergence guarantee for sufficiently wide smooth-activation fully connected networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient overparameterization permits provable interpolation by gradient descent in deep smooth networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper obtains polynomial depth dependence in sufficient convergence conditions for explicitly scaled residual architectures, compared with exponential depth dependence in its plain-network bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaled residual connections improve the depth dependence of this analysis's sufficient width and convergence bounds; these bounds do not establish necessary requirements or observed depth degradation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97, 2019)
record.problems: The paper itself says it focuses on training loss and does not address test loss; realistic networks’ widths are much smaller than the theoretical requirement, and the analysis covers gradient descent rather than stochastic gradient descent. The results are proofs, not empirical tests on the benchmark settings in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported result omitted. Results in related-work citations were excluded because they are not this paper’s own results.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error with SGD or Adam, including corrupted labels, and the effects of smaller models, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Actual training-error degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the special-initialization exceptions.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and initialization on learning speed or trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics around the initial stability limit, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's verdicts. Untested benchmarks and recipes do not justify limits_scope, and a weaker sufficient bound for plain networks does not show that their training actually degrades with depth. Row states here describe whether the rows determine a supplied version, not whether the convergence theorems hold.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random labels on those benchmarks, SGD or Adam, or smaller models and early stopping.

Does not empirically compare plain and residual convolutional networks or measure training error versus depth on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; its fully connected and residual architectures are theoretical and differ from the standard ResNet described in the version.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural network
rows.size_stated: width m = Ω(2^O(H) max{n⁴/λmin(K(H))⁴, n² log(Hn/δ)/λmin(K(H))², n²/δ, n log(Hn/δ)/δ})
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained all layers by gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5.1 gives a linear-rate training-loss bound for gradient descent with an appropriately small constant step size.

conditions.value: fully-connected feedforward network with H hidden layers
unit-norm inputs; |yi| = O(1); non-parallel inputs for positive definiteness
weight entries and output layer sampled from standard Gaussian

rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The theorem states convergence to zero loss at a linear rate in the limit; this is a theoretical least-squares result, not an empirical classification benchmark.
rows.check: Valid theoretical convergence result, but fully connected squared-loss training does not measure V1's convolutional classification behavior or V3's depth degradation. Exponential depth dependence in a sufficient bound is not evidence that deeper networks attain higher training error; Section 4, footnote 7 explicitly cautions against that inference. The extracted width formula also does not faithfully reproduce Theorem 5.1's three-term maximum.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.size_stated: width m as specified in Theorem 6.1; polynomial in n, H, and data-dependent parameters
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained all layers by gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 6.1 gives a linear-rate training-loss bound for the paper’s residual architecture, which has skip connections at every layer.

conditions.value: ResNet with skip connections at every layer
unit-norm inputs; |yi| = O(1); non-parallel inputs for positive definiteness
weight entries and output layer sampled from standard Gaussian

rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The paper says width and convergence rate are polynomial in n and H. The theorem concerns its theoretical residual architecture and least-squares loss.
rows.check: The theorem guarantees squared-loss convergence for a fully connected residual architecture with explicit depth-dependent residual scaling. It does not measure V1's convolutional classification error or compare actual training errors of shallower plain, deeper plain, and residual networks as V3 requires.

rows.subject: convolutional ResNet
rows.size_stated: width m as specified in Theorem 7.1; polynomial in n, p, H, and data-dependent parameters
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained all layers by gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 7.1 gives a linear-rate training-loss bound for convolutional ResNet.

conditions.value: unit Frobenius-norm inputs; |yi| = O(1); non-degenerate data
weight entries and output layer sampled from standard Gaussian

rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The theorem states convergence for convolutional ResNet; the paper does not report benchmark classification runs.
rows.check: The convolutional residual theorem concerns squared-loss convergence for abstract data under large-width assumptions. It supplies no CIFAR classification results with SGD or Adam, and no plain-network depth comparison. Its valid convergence guarantee cannot determine the stated versions' effects.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Theoretical fully-connected, residual, and convolutional residual networks under the stated smooth-activation, width, data, and step-size assumptions
reader_labels.reason: The theorems give linear-rate convergence of training loss to zero for randomly initialized gradient descent (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Empirical classification benchmarks and practical training recipes
reader_labels.reason: The paper proves least-squares convergence under large-width assumptions but does not test CIFAR classification, random-label benchmark experiments, SGD, Adam, or early stopping (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The paper’s theoretical fully-connected and residual architectures
reader_labels.reason: The authors report exponential depth dependence in width and step size for fully-connected networks, versus polynomial dependence for their residual architecture; this is not an empirical plain-versus-shortcut convolutional comparison (R1–R2).
